- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., post-80+ peaks, model jumps to 82+ while true settles at 81+).
- Underestimate downward corrections when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.5+), especially in early 30d forecasts — model often misses sharp drops.
- Overshoots in early forecast days (e.g., day 1–3) when sentiment is volatile or negative — model reacts too aggressively to recent lows.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect after strong upward moves, especially if sentiment is weak (e.g., -0.3 to 0.0), leading to over-forecasted peaks.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model delays correction — overestimates recovery until later days.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts often overestimate mid-term volatility — model assumes momentum persists longer than actual mean reversion.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.4+ over 5+ days), reduce forecast slope — avoid upward bias in 30d horizon.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model tends to overreact — cap forecast rise to 1–2% above prior peak unless sentiment is strong.
